context: Calendar heatmap data visualization showing daily temperature departures from normal across three cities (Chicago, London, Singapore) for 2024, with annotated weather events.
first_impression: A clean, well-structured calendar heatmap with a deliberately chosen Tol-inspired diverging palette and narrative annotations that elevate it above generic charting.
what_works: The custom blue-white-red palette (#4477AA → white → #EE6677) is intentional and colorblind-friendly, and the annotated leader lines calling out the polar vortex and heat wave events add genuine storytelling value. Typographic hierarchy is clear — bold title, lighter subtitle, weighted city labels, and quiet axis ticks all feel considered.
what_doesnt: Day-of-week labels appear only on the London panel and only for alternating days (Mon/Wed/Fri), making the calendar grid harder to orient on Chicago and Singapore. The month boundary step-cut paths render as short, faint disconnected segments that read as visual clutter rather than clean dividers.
